name: Cyclic Pianos
what: A playable keyboard whose keys are the vertices of a cycle or of a Möbius ladder, with anywhere up to 24 notes to the octave. The black-key set is chosen to minimise energy on the underlying graph, and the geometry of whatever you are playing is drawn live beside the keys. It will also read a MIDI file and play it back on the current tuning, naming the chords and scrolling the score as it goes.

name: Cyclic Sequences
what: Companion page to the Bridges 2026 work: minimum-energy sets on cycles and Möbius ladders, and the sequences the keyboards are built from.

name: Mathematical genealogy
what: My advisor graph, back through Bollobás, Erdős, Fejér, Weierstraß and Gauß to seventeenth-century Leipzig. Click anyone to light up every path from them down to me. It is a graph and not a tree, which is the fun of it.

name: Möbius piano strips
what: Two-sided printable Möbius band keyboards with duplex registration and parameterised key layouts, including an all-white version for students to fill in themselves.

name: Mathematical Rhythms

what: Four floating percussion panels, each playing the minimum-energy onset set on a cycle or a Möbius ladder. Drag the graph to change the number of pulses and strikes; pull the centre arc to rotate. Runs offline on a tablet.
